decision: A monitor-owned checkpoint writer must publish a fresh, exact-profile, exact-run checkpoint before the TUI renders. The repaired launcher now enforces that boundary.
problem_restatement: When monitor mode found no active checkpoint writer, it started one and immediately rendered the TUI. A first refresh can take approximately two minutes, so the cockpit could temporarily show stale or missing data despite a healthy live backend.

root_cause.failure_mode: The TUI consumed the prior or absent checkpoint while the recovered writer was still building its first exact checkpoint.
root_cause.capital_effect: none observed; the TUI and checkpoint writer are report-only and cannot submit orders
root_cause.observability_effect: temporary missing or stale cockpit data

implemented_repair.writer_exit_behavior: fail closed before TUI render with the exact exit code and checkpoint log path
implemented_repair.timeout_behavior: fail closed after the configured startup timeout
implemented_repair.external_writer_behavior: unchanged; an already active fresh writer is reused and is not stopped when the TUI exits

validation.red_evidence: The new ordering regression observed start,tui,stop and failed because wait was absent.

recommendation.recommendation: Use the unchanged v52 monitor command; on a future missing-writer recovery, allow startup to wait for exact fresh telemetry before the cockpit appears.
recommendation.why_now: The prior behavior directly explains a recurrent missing-data window and undermines the continuous research cockpit.
recommendation.evidence_reviewed: Launcher control flow, writer lock behavior, checkpoint logs, exact runtime identities, red-green tests, broader launcher regressions, and a real attach/quit probe.
recommendation.observed_problem_or_opportunity: The display could start before recovered telemetry was ready.
recommendation.alternatives_considered: Ignore the startup gap, add arbitrary sleep, keep the TUI coupled to a stale artifact, or wait on the existing exact freshness validator.
recommendation.expected_upside: Eliminate the known startup interval in which the cockpit can render missing or stale checkpoint data.
recommendation.main_risks_and_failure_modes: A genuinely slow rebuild can delay TUI startup up to the configured timeout; an active external writer that later dies remains the independent supervisor's responsibility.
recommendation.validation_completed: Freshness ordering, retry, writer exit, active-writer reuse, staged identity, accounting identity, launcher regression, formatting, file limits, and real attach/quit behavior.
recommendation.validation_still_required: Observe the next real recovery from an absent writer and confirm the TUI appears only after the first fresh checkpoint.
recommendation.success_metrics: No TUI render precedes a fresh matching checkpoint when monitor mode starts its own writer.
recommendation.failure_or_rollback_triggers: A TUI appears with stale data after recovered-writer startup, a foreign run/profile is accepted, an external writer is duplicated, or the repair changes backend lifecycle.
recommendation.confidence_level: high on the diagnosed startup ordering defect and repair; medium on eliminating every future missing-data cause because independent writer crashes remain separately monitored

falsifier: Reopen the diagnosis if a fresh exact checkpoint exists before launch yet the correctly sized TUI still omits backend data, or if a recovered writer reaches freshness but the launcher does not proceed.
